summary: Lower Néguac's range lights, moved from Tabusintac Gully in 1891, guided ships in Miramichi Bay from 1892. Automated 1957; the rear light went dark in 2003.

structures.note: Rowlett: 8 m (28 ft) square pyramidal wood tower with lantern and gallery. Lighthouse Friends: 33 ft (about 10 m) from base to the lantern vane. Lighthouse Digest: 28 ft tower, 35 ft focal plane. The sources disagree.
Lens lantern on a 16 ft (5 m) mast with a shed, 1892; new mast and shed 1896 (Lighthouse Friends). Rowlett and Lighthouse Digest describe a small skeletal tower on the wharf.

access.note: Site and tower closed, private property (Rowlett; Lighthouse Digest). Lighthouse Friends: owned by the Canadian Coast Guard, grounds and tower closed.

events.note: Abandoned Tabusintac Gully range lights moved to Lower Néguac in October 1891 (W. H. Noble, $205.07)
Range lights activated with the opening of navigation in 1892
Front light changed to fixed red and raised 3 m (10 ft)
New mast and shed for the front light, about 14 m (45 ft) south-west of the old site, light 7.6 m (25 ft) above high water
Rear light moved to a newly purchased site 366 m (1,200 ft) from the wharf light
Lighthouse Digest says the structure was altered in 1929 and 1935; no detail given
Range automated; last keeper Zeph J. Savoy served until then
Rear light decommissioned at the end of the 2003 season; the status of the wharf light is disputed

corrections.why: The range lit at this site in 1892. The 1873 date in the record is Rowlett's 'station established 1873'. Lighthouse Friends dates the 1873 tower and beacon to Tabusintac Gully, moved here in October 1891, and the 1873 Neguac Sandbar light is a separate light.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1873 and 1892 dates belong to different lights. Lighthouse Friends places the 1873 tower and beacon at Tabusintac Gully and says they moved to Lower Néguac in October 1891; the range was activated with the opening of navigation in 1892. Rowlett gives 1892 with 1873 as the station-established year.

notes_for_editor: (1) Keeper match: 'Mcintosh, Chas' against 'Lower Neguac Wharf Lights' in the 1904 statement was matched by OCR column position. Checked on the page image (printed p. 159, scan p. 172): the row reads McIntosh, Chas | Lower Neguac Wharf Lights | Dec. 19, 1892 | 100.00, and the McLennan / Escuminac row sits on the same line. The 1905 statement (printed p. 260, scan p. 341) gives the station name 'Lower Neguac Wharf Lights', checked on the image. The 1901 statement (printed p. 148, scan p. 259) gives the row 'McIntosh, Chas | Neguac Range Lights | Dec. 19, 1892', checked on the image. (2) Rear tower height disagrees: Lighthouse Friends 33 ft (about 10 m) to the lantern vane; Rowlett 8 m (28 ft); Lighthouse Digest 28 ft tower and 35 ft focal plane. No height is stored in the structure record; the story gives the disagreement. (3) Front light status disagrees: Rowlett says it has been deactivated; Lighthouse Friends says an official light is still exhibited from the wharf. The story reports both. (4) Heritage: the record's Canadian Register 13044 (2006 designation) and Federal Heritage Building 11730 entries could not be read. historicplaces.ca and pc.gc.ca returned no text through fetch_text, so heritage status is unverified and left out of the story. (5) Lighthouse Friends gives visibility as 'nine miles' and 'ten miles' without saying nautical; no nautical figure is used. (6) The 1915 and 1918 Canadian statements list 'Lower Neguac' among works ('Erection of wooden range-light towers'; 'Old back light tower moved'). The OCR prints station names and works in separate column blocks, so the works could not be matched to this station by position. They are not used. (7) The 1891 move, the 1892 lighting, the 1895 and 1896 changes, the 1929 move and automation in 1957 rest on Lighthouse Friends alone; the corpus does not reach those years in the Canadian series. (8) Chronicling America returned no pages for 'Lower Neguac' (1880-1930) or 'Neguac' with lighthouse. No wreck, storm or rescue tied to this range turned up in the sources read, so the Storms chapter is left out. (9) Lighthouse Friends spells Tabusintac 'Taubsintac' once; that quotation is kept as printed, and the story uses 'Tabusintac'. (10) Flickr posts that say the tower was built on Crab Island and moved in 1929 are second-hand and not cited. (11) The record's 1873 first_lit is corrected to 1892 for this site; see corrections. The 1873 Neguac Sandbar light is a separate station. (12) Fiscal years: the 1902, 1905 and 1906 volumes state their fiscal years ended 30 June, as footnoted. (13) Verification pass 2026-10-27: the opening 'through the channel at the bay's mouth' was not in any source and was removed; 'these gullies' (Tabusintac is a separate gully) was corrected; 'about 150' is 150 in the source; the 'most sources' remark now names the two sources that spell the name without the accent.
